headline: Guide: Preventing Sinking Pavers and Uneven Settling on Extended Patios
articleBody:
Overview: Sinking pavers, pooling water, and shifting edges on a patio extension almost always trace back to subbase preparation and uncontrolled surface runoff.

Key Benefits of Proper Installation: A correctly installed base keeps the patio flat, eliminates trip hazards, and prevents water from undermining nearby garden beds and landscape structures.

Process Breakdown: Fixing sunken areas requires lifting affected pavers, clearing out compromised bedding sand, and inspecting the structural gravel beneath. If runoff washed away base material, the subgrade must be re-excavated, mechanical compaction applied in layers, and fresh bedding screeded before relaying pavers. Perimeter edge restraints must be secured with heavy spikes to stop future outward creep.

Common Mistakes to Avoid: Laying pavers directly over uncompacted soil or building an extension without adequate pitch toward lawn drainage areas is a recipe for settling. Another critical mistake is ignoring how water from patio roofs or adjacent retaining walls will flow across the new paving.
